title: What is known about 1RB0LF_1LC1RA_0RE0RD_---1LE_1LF1RC_1LC1LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LF_1LC1RA_0RE0RD_---1LE_1LF1RC_1LC1LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open, Collatz-like, reduced in Lean to a number question. It is a Lean theorem (kernel-checked, no native_decide) that the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of the block 144 under an explicit arithmetic map F hits a halting value: a block 1t with t = 2j+1 − 2j − 7 (3, 17, 47, 109, 235, …), or a restart state of the same form. The orbit misses them for its first 10,000 resets (t reaches about 3,900 bits), and a random-orbit heuristic makes a hit very unlikely; whether it ever hits is open.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 37,702 cells have been visited and 19,263 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.146). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.509).

claims.title: The sweep rule
claims.text: From (01)n+3 (11)m+1 with the head in B at the right end, the machine reaches (01)n+1 12m+8 in 8m + 18 steps, for all n, m (and a second form of the same sweep in state A). Found and proved by bbtools.cycles.

claims.title: The leaf rules of the reset
claims.text: Thirteen rules for all parameter values, found and proved by bbtools.symtm.prove: the sweep (10)x+212y+1 A> → (10)x12y+7 A>, the even reset 12k+6 A> → (10)k+117 A>, the start of the odd reset 12k+7 A> → C> 0 12k+14, the start, one step and the four possible ends of a doubling round, the restart, and the halting configuration.

claims.title: The reset map
claims.text: An explicit computable map F on states z t (the block 1<sup>t</sup> with A after it) and rs d (the rounds of the odd reset starting over): F s = some s' means the machine goes from s to s' in at least one step, F s = none means it halts from s. The inductions over the sweeps, over the steps of a round and over the rounds are proved by hand; the six blocks t ≤ 5 by evaluation.

claims.title: Halts iff the orbit of 44 hits H
claims.text: The machine halts from blank tape iff the orbit of z 44 under F reaches a state in H, where H is z t with t + 2s + 11 = 2<sup>s+3</sup> for some s (t = 2<sup>j+1</sup> − 2j − 7) and rs d with d + s + 4 = 2<sup>s+2</sup>. Blank tape is z 0, and F takes it to z 19 and then z 44.

claims.title: No halt in the first 300 resets
claims.text: The orbit of z 44 has no halting state among its first 300 resets, evaluated by the kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 resets
claims.text: The same for 10,000 resets (t then has about 3,900 bits), by compiled evaluation.

claims.title: The orbit probably never hits H
claims.text: In each doubling band (H<sub>j-1</sub>, H<sub>j</sub>] only one odd value halts, the bands double in width and t grows by a factor of about 1.3 per reset, so the expected number of future hits is far below 1.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known: whether the orbit of 44 under F ever hits H, a Collatz-like question about one explicit orbit.

explainer.lede: Probably not, but nobody can prove it: between rare resets this machine is a plain bouncer, and Lean now proves that it halts exactly when one explicit Collatz-like orbit hits a sparse set of numbers.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 37,702 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
Proved in Lean: halting from blank tape is exactly the orbit question for the map F, H = {2<sup>j+1</sup>−2j−7}.
No halting value among the first 10,000 resets of the orbit (the first 300 by the kernel).

sections.heading: A bouncer trading 01s for 1s
html: At the moments the head, in state A, stands on the blank cell just right of the tape, the tape is always of the form (10)x 1y: a block of 10 pairs on the left and a solid block of 1s on the right (y odd). One sweep (the head runs left to the pairs, turns, and comes back) removes two pairs and adds six 1s:

This is a theorem in Lean for all x and y (w_sweep). The pairs are a fuel tank: after x/2 sweeps the tape is a solid block 1t A> (call it Z(t)); with x even t = y + 3x, with x odd t = y + 3x + 2 (w_to_z).

sections.heading: The reset: an explicit map, proved
html:
What happens to a solid block Z(t) depends on t:

  • t even: one pass turns the 1s back into pairs, 12k+6 → (10)k+1 17, and the sweeps run again.
  • t odd: the head turns the block into C> 0 1t+7 at the left end and runs doubling rounds: a block of 01 pairs at the left end eats 1s and doubles each round, (01)2, (01)6, (01)14, (01)30, … (2r+1 − 2 pairs after r rounds). Inside a round, pairs move one at a time from the old block to the new one, and each move costs two 1s.

The last round runs out of 1s, and how many it has left decides everything: if exactly one 1 is left at the start of a round the head reads blank tape in state D and the machine halts; with a few more it leaves a smaller bouncer (10)x 1y, or a block Z(4i+4), or (one value per band) the rounds start over once from a block of 01s. Following the counts gives the exact halting values t = 2j+1 − 2j − 7 = 3, 17, 47, 109, 235, 489, …

All of this is a Lean theorem now: thirteen leaf rules found and proved by the symbolic simulator (lean/Leaves.lean), and hand-written inductions over the sweeps, the steps of a round and the rounds that assemble them into the map F (lean/Reset.lean, F_sem).

sections.heading: What halting would require
html: Proved in Lean (halts_iff_H): the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of 44 under F reaches a halting value t = 2j+1 − 2j − 7 (or a restart state of the same form). The orbit misses them for 10,000 resets (t up to about 23900). Only one odd value in each doubling band halts and the orbit grows by about 1.3× per reset, so a hit is very unlikely, but proving that it never happens means controlling one explicit orbit of a Collatz-like map, which nobody knows how to do: the machine stays open, Collatz-like.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.146). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.509).
After 109 steps the tape spans 37,702 cells (229 left of the start, 26,616 right), with a density of 1s of 0.511.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Bouncer whose tape is (10)^x 1^y: each sweep trades two pairs for six 1s; when the pairs run out the block 1^t is recycled by an explicit map, and it is a Lean theorem that the machine halts iff the orbit of 44 hits t = 2^(j+1) - 2j - 7.
family: two-region bouncer with a Collatz-like reset
